comments.author: @goedelite
comments.text: Expansively presented - too expansively.  Expatriats need more detailed information about the quality of life for newcomers.  For example,  I have watched videos whose presenter found that rental apartment lack large appliances (washers, dryers, kitchen stoves, refrigerators.)     I have listened to newcomers who found that many buildings were not built with insulation; that one must shiver through a winter in one's own apartment, constantly wearing sweaters and a hat INDOORS!   Besides taxes to the government, which may be modest,  one will be charge a "community" tax along with rent.   I don't know how reasonable these are.  One cannot apply for residency from abroad.  For this reason, it is necessary to maintain two residences, one abroad and one in the "old" country.  That also entails many round trips by air for most expats before being able to relocate permanently.  For newcomers who do not speak Spanish, relocating, applying for residency, providing documents is particularly expensive - requiring legal assistance and document translation.   A country that wishes to increase its middle-class population from abroad should make relocating easier !

replies.author: @PrimeTravel2

replies.author: @marcosreverberi5555
replies.text:
​​@PrimeTravel2This is a phonetic matter: 'mate' here is written by spanish speaking people. Read in spanish, the five vowels have just five sounds, just /'mate/.  
But the /a/ sound is similar to the 'u' for the english "cup" . 
For the five written vowels, we have precisely five sounds: just by reading a word you know the exact pronunciation. 
Or just by pronouncing something, you can know how to write it.
